title: Context eviction playbook — personal notes
content:
Quick brain dump: context eviction and session sizing playbook. Personal scratchpad for possible heuristics, tradeoffs, and experiments. Not polished — throwing ideas here to share with Maya/Zeke before a sync.

Problem statement:
- Sessions accumulate prefixes + KV caches + embeddings across time. For heavy users, this drives memory pressure and increases per-request CPU/GPU work, pushing up cost and sometimes causing latency spikes.
- We need a simple, predictable eviction strategy that preserves high-value context (recent turns and important references) while reducing token cost and memory footprint.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce average memory per active session by ~30% for heavy-tail users without degrading perceived quality (evaluated by small human/eval set).
- Keep tail-latency SLO violations unchanged or improved.
- Provide clear knobs for product (time-based TTLs, priority tags) and safe defaults for hosted customers.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Avoid heavy compute per-request for eviction decisions (no large semantic similarity across the whole history on every request).
- Support both hosted API and Dedicated private deployments with minimal config differences.
- This doc focuses on in-memory session eviction; persistent archival/long-term store is a separate effort.

Rough taxonomy of candidate heuristics:
1) Time-based TTL + size cap (baseline)
   - Keep N most recent tokens/turns OR cap session memory to M bytes, evict oldest when exceeded.
   - Pros: simple, predictable, easy to explain to customers.
   - Cons: may evict semantically important older references used intermittently.

2) LRU at turn or message granularity
   - Track last-accessed timestamp per turn/message; evict least recently used.
   - Pros: good for interactive sessions where recent things matter.
   - Cons: needs bookkeeping; corner cases when system replays historical content for compression.

3) Priority tagging + soft TTLs
   - Allow upstream to tag segments with priority (high/medium/low). Each priority has its own TTL and weight in eviction scoring. SDKs can expose an API to attach a priority label.
   - Pros: gives product control and explicit preservation of important bits.
   - Cons: requires SDK adoption; risk of misuse (everything high).

4) Lightweight semantic anchors (cheap embedding signatures)
   - Compute compact signatures (e.g., 64-d quantized embed or minhash) for turns on write. Maintain a small cache of "anchors" reflective of currently used semantics. Evict turns whose signatures are distant from recent anchors.
   - Pros: can preserve semantically relevant older context without heavy compute.
   - Cons: extra storage and logic; we need to tune distance thresholds; may be noisy for short queries.

5) Hybrid: LRU + priority + sampling-based semantic check
   - Use LRU/TTL as the main mechanism. On eviction candidates that cross a threshold, occasionally (sampled) run a fast semantic check against recent queries to decide final eviction. This keeps CPU costs bounded but prevents common false evictions.

User stories (high level):
- As a product engineer, I want predictable cost per session so I can estimate bills and plan capacity.
- As an end user, I want the assistant to remember important project details across multi-day sessions.
- As an ops engineer, I want a knob to favor latency (aggressive eviction) or quality (conservative eviction) during incidents.

Metrics to track / experiment readouts:
- Memory per active session (bytes) by percentile (50/75/90/99).
- Per-request median and 95/99th latency.
- Token generation cost per 1k requests.
- Eval-quality: on a curated prompt set, measure BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity or human score change when we apply eviction.
- Eviction-induced misses: percentage of requests that had to rehydrate archived content.

Experiment plan (phase 0 -> 2):
- Phase 0: Baseline measurement: collect current session growth curves, top-k users by session size, and eviction-free cost profile. Instrument per-turn last-access and keep raw data for analysis. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: Implement TTL + size cap (configurable) behind a feature flag in hosted API. Run A/B on small % of traffic and measure metrics above. (3 weeks)
- Phase 2: Implement priority tags in SDK alpha + LRU bookkeeping. Run internal tests with Solutions Eng and one pilot customer. (4–6 weeks)
- Phase 3: Prototype lightweight anchors and sampled semantic checks; if useful, roll into hybrid default. (4 weeks)

Operational knobs and API considerations:
- Server-side config: global default TTL, session-size limit, per-tenant overrides.
- SDK option: attach priority label and optional 'pin' TTL for a turn. Example: send({ text, priority: 'high', pin_for_seconds: 86400 }).
- Admin API: force-evict-session(session_id) and get-session-metrics(session_id).
- Telemetry: emit eviction events with reason (ttl/size/lru/priority) for downstream cost attribution.

UX / customer expectations:
- Need to document expected defaults and how to request longer retention. Clear messages in Console when sessions are evicted due to size.
- For Dedicated/private customers allow more permissive defaults or provide an offline archiver.

Risks / open questions:
- How to quantify "perceived quality" reliably for multi-turn assistants? We need a small human eval harness that can be run regularly.
- Sampling strategy: what percentage of evictions should trigger a semantic check to get good signal without high CPU? Start with 1% and iterate.
- Storage and cost of embedding signatures: what's the ballpark overhead per turn? (ask Applied ML)
- Abuse: customers may set all turns to high priority. Consider quota on total pinned tokens per session/tenant.

Next steps (TODOs):
- [ ] Josh to add instrumentation ticket for per-turn last-access and session-size metrics (INF-1245) — assigned.
- [ ] Maya to prototype TTL+size cap in dev environment and surface dashboards.
- [ ] Zeke to propose minimal wire format for priority labels in SDK and draft SDK change.
- [ ] I will draft a short Confluence page summarizing the playbook + rollout checklist.

Notes for sync with Maya/Zeke (agenda):
- Share baseline numbers and top-10 sessions by memory.
- Decide initial default TTL and size cap (conservative vs aggressive).
- Confirm telemetry schema for eviction events.

Random thoughts / heuristics I like:
- Weighted eviction score = alpha * age_score + beta * inverse_access_score + gamma * (1 - pinned) + delta * semantic_distance_score. Keep alpha/beta/gamma constants tunable per-tenant.
- Small "recall window": when rehydrating archived content, prefer compressed summaries (1–2 sentence) kept in the session, rather than full rehydration, to guard latency.

End of dump. Will clean up after syncing and turn into PRD draft if we decide on a strategy.
